### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **146** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 775a0006bddbf7a1afc88b3a83e52cc0eea96711` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `72b207b93a8f3ce0af5e434ef441903042a24314` — the merge of head `eff10df553173382ac5f2164b152375803ad4214` into base `775a0006bddbf7a1afc88b3a83e52cc0eea96711`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 72b207b93a8f3ce0af5e434ef441903042a24314 && git checkout 72b207b93a8f3ce0af5e434ef441903042a24314
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 775a0006bddbf7a1afc88b3a83e52cc0eea96711 eff10df553173382ac5f2164b152375803ad4214 && git checkout -B drift-repro 775a0006bddbf7a1afc88b3a83e52cc0eea96711 && git merge --no-ff eff10df553173382ac5f2164b152375803ad4214

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 775a0006bddbf7a1afc88b3a83e52cc0eea96711
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2c2ade72c8b717a8a51d357648570e4b7224660e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/export.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts, packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/ImportWizard.tsx

### ① Derived judgments

1. Accept set: widening only, named right. `ImportRowResultSchema` is a plain `z.object` with no `.strict()`, so before this head an `errors` key was stripped and after it the key is kept. Nothing is refused that parsed before: the only new refusal is an `errors` element that is not `{ field, code, message }`, and no server sends `errors` today. `ImportResponseSchema.results` and `ImportJobResultsSchema.results` carry it through the shared row schema. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is the right arm. Correct.

2. Consumers typed by the row: none breaks. `packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts:79` keeps its own `ImportRowResult` interface, not derived from the schema, so core compiles unchanged; REST serves core's rows and has no parse path through the schema (`packages/rest/src/import-row-schema-drift-20701.test.ts` reads keys by name). `packages/client/src/index.ts:7136` types the answer as `ImportResponse` and only unwraps it. `ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/ImportWizard.tsx:558` reads only the row's `field`, `error` and `code` (a Pick of those three) and `:908` dedupes on `result.field`; both still read element 0's answer. `plugin-auth` `IdentityImportRowResult extends ImportRowResult` and `app-shell` intersect it; an optional key added to the base is additive for both. `type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts:509` holds because `ValidateDataIssueSchema` has no default or transform (input equals infer), which `warnings` already proved. Correct.

3. Element shape: reusing `ValidateDataIssueSchema` is right. Its required members are exactly the ruling's `{ field, code, message }`; the same row's `warnings` and the validate verdict's row `errors` (`protocol.zod.ts:2607`) already use it for errors, so there is precedent for an error list carrying the advisory-only `rule` and `severity` as optional. The cost is small and real: the generated nested-shape table in export.mdx now says `rule` and `severity` are "present only on an advisory rule hit" under `ImportRowResult.errors[number]`, and nothing in the describe says a cell error is never such a hit. The docblock says it, but docblocks do not reach `gen:docs`. One sentence in the `errors` describe ("an element never carries `rule` or `severity`") would make the docs honest. Minor, not a FAIL.

4. The element-0 invariant is stated in a way the runner can keep only on one of its failed-row paths. At origin/main the runner fills a failed row from four sources: `coerceRow` cell errors (`:1221`, where `error` is `errors[0].message`, so the invariant holds); a duplicate or ambiguous match key (no cells, so the describe's "omits it" clause covers it); a rejecting validate verdict (`:1293`, where `error` is `composeValidationMessage(verdict.errors)`, every finding joined by "; ", `field` is omitted when the first finding has none, and `code` falls back to `VALIDATION_FAILED`); and a refused write via `toFailedResult` / `adoptDoorVerdict` (`error` is the door's sentence). On the last two, filling `errors` would break "`error` names element 0". The describe says "present only on a failed row that has at least one cell error" but never says which list fills it. The ruling's scope is cell errors and the card names `coerceRow` as the producer, so the contract is keepable under option A. Finding: the describe should name the source (the coercion's cell errors), so a verdict-row fill is visibly a spec change and not a quiet drift. Carried with the respin below, not a FAIL on its own.

5. Docs: `content/docs/references/api/export.mdx` at head matches the zod describes in all three row tables (ImportJobResults.results, ImportResponse.results, ImportRowResult) and adds the `ImportRowResult.errors[number]` nested shape in the right place. The `check:generated --reconcile-only` lane (lint.yml:5293) was still in progress at review time, so freshness is not confirmed by CI yet.

6. Tests: the seven new pins assert the key survives a parse (not bare `success`), element identity with `ValidateDataIssueSchema` and the `warnings` element, refusal at `['errors', 0, 'message']`, and the type. The element-0 test pins agreement on a conforming row only; no refine enforces it, which is right, since a refine would be a narrowing.

### ② Semver level

FAIL. The changeset grades `@objectstack/spec` `patch` with `Metadata-protocol: none`, and the PR moves `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json` (adds `api/ImportRowResult:errors`). `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs:2055` refuses exactly this: a declared `none` over a moved authorable-surface shard is verdict `none-baseline-moved`, exit 1, remedy "declare `Metadata-protocol: added` and grade the package at least `minor`; a baseline is never edited to quiet this gate". The head's `Check Changeset` check-run is red with that annotation (run 40449099225, job 122007327584). The dev report wrote the check as in_progress at report time; it has since failed.

Precedent agrees with the gate: the `warnings` widening of this same schema was graded `minor` (packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md, section at line 16392), and the last three commits that moved `authorable-surface/api.json` on main (b77bb37e, f1ddace8, f4112a70) all declared `Metadata-protocol: added`.

Byte-for-byte agreement: the PR body, the changeset and claim 6433227708 all read `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. They agree with each other and are all wrong. The claim is the dispatch's own line; the dev copied it. Note the ruling's phrase "零元数据键" (no new authored key) is about authored metadata, and the ratchet still records `api/ImportRowResult:*` keys, so the gate is the arbiter here.

Respin needed: changeset `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, `Metadata-protocol: added`, in the changeset, the PR body and a fresh claim line on the card.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open question (dev, verdict rows): answered in ① item 4. Option A for #25582's first cut is right and is the ruling's scope. Add to this PR's `errors` describe that the list is the coercion's cell errors, so the runner can keep the element-0 invariant and a later verdict fill is a declared spec change.
- Describe honesty on `rule` / `severity`: one sentence in the `errors` describe, as in ① item 3. Same respin.
- No refine for "present only on a failed row": agreed, a refine would narrow.
- `check:dev-prereqs` red locally: local-only family, judges workspace state, not this diff. Agreed.
- The dev's 7 NOT-MEASURED derived families all run in CI on this head: `check:doc-formula-expressions` (lint.yml:6472), `check:doc-security-posture` (lint.yml:6479), spec `check:skill-examples` (lint.yml:6465), `check:docs-transcript-drift` (lint.yml:5780), `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (ci.yml:2941), `check:lean-entry-closure` (ci.yml:2965), `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` (lint.yml:3931). Their lanes were in progress at review time.
- Check-runs at review: 42 on the head; 1 failure (Check Changeset), 8 Test Core shards, Build Core, Build UI Deps, Build Docs and 10 Lint and Type Check lanes still in progress; the rest success or skipped. Not all green.
- Author: PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no non-fleet login to name.
- UI: the console still shows only element 0 (ImportWizard reads `field` / `error` / `code`). The business reason on #25582 is met at the wire only; a UI card to read `errors` is outside this card and the ruling.

## Contract review — addendum to record 6433766607 (FAIL at prior head 2c2ade72)

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `eff10df553173382ac5f2164b152375803ad4214`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/export.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts, packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/ImportWizard.tsx, .changeset/26425-import-row-every-cell-error.md, content/docs/references/api/export.mdx

This addendum judges the delta from the prior head 2c2ade72 to this head against the two findings of PR comment 6433766607; the ① judgments of that record stand unless an item below says otherwise.

### ① Derived judgments

1. Delta inventory: one commit, three files, 9 insertions and 7 deletions: the changeset (grade and `Metadata-protocol` line, plus one sentence in its prose), `packages/spec/src/api/export.zod.ts` (two string fragments inside the `errors` describe, no other token) and `content/docs/references/api/export.mdx` (the same sentence in the three `errors` rows). `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json` is unchanged in the delta, so the moved shard is still exactly `api/ImportRowResult:errors`; `packages/spec/src/api/export.test.ts`, `protocol.zod.ts`, `import-runner.ts` and `ImportWizard.tsx` are untouched. No schema member, type, default, refine or test moved, so prior items 1, 2 and 6 (accept set is widening only; no row-typed consumer breaks; the seven pins) hold unchanged. Correct.

2. Prior finding (2), describe honesty and source: met. The `errors` describe now reads, in the middle, "The list holds the import's cell-coercion errors, and a cell error never carries the advisory-only `rule` or `severity`." That names the producer (the coercion's cell errors, `coerceRow` at `import-runner.ts:1221`, where `error` equals `errors[0].message`) and states the `rule`/`severity` absence the docblock had kept to itself. With the source named, the element-0 invariant is keepable on the only path that fills the list, and a later fill from a verdict row (`:1293`, `composeValidationMessage`) or a refused write is a visible spec change, which is what prior item 4 asked for. The nested-shape table `ImportRowResult.errors[number]` in export.mdx still says `rule` and `severity` are "present only on an advisory rule hit": that is `ValidateDataIssueSchema`'s own member describe, shared with `warnings` and the validate verdict, and the row-level sentence now says a cell error is never such a hit, so the two tables read consistently. Correct.

3. Generated docs match the describe: the describe string assembled from the four concatenated fragments at this head occurs verbatim in all three `errors` rows of `content/docs/references/api/export.mdx` at this head (the ImportJobResults.results, ImportResponse.results and ImportRowResult tables; compared by reading both files from the committed tree, no generator run). Prior item 5 is now confirmed on the committed tree rather than only claimed; the CI `check:generated` lane result is in ③.

4. Prior finding (1), byte-for-byte agreement of the declaration lines: met. Changeset at head: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`. PR body (GitHub REST, `pulls/26454`, updated 04:36:22Z): `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`, and its "What changes" prose says `minor` with `Metadata-protocol: added`. Claim amendment 6433776664 on #26425 (04:29:38Z): `Metadata-protocol: added`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. Clause-② is unchanged on all three carriers, as required. Correct.

### ② Semver level

PASS. `minor` with `Metadata-protocol: added` is the grade `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` asks for over a moved authorable-surface shard, and it matches the `warnings` precedent on this same schema. The head's `Check Changeset` first ran at 04:33:13Z to 04:34:58Z against the pre-edit PR body and failed with the `none-baseline-moved` annotation (its metadata-protocol line read `Metadata-protocol: none`, the body's text at that minute, while the changeset already said `added`). The body was edited at 04:36:22Z and `Check Changeset` re-ran on this same head (job 122012337961, run 40450661111, 04:36:28Z to 04:38:08Z): success, no failure annotation. The earlier red job stays listed on the head's check-runs as a completed failure; the newest run of that check is green. Nothing in the delta changes the ① accept-set judgment, so the arm stays `yes (widening)`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Prior ③ answers stand: option A for #25582 is now written into the describe; no refine; `check:dev-prereqs` local-only; UI card outside this card.
- Dev open questions on the respin: none new. The body's "Acceptance notes" restate option A with the describe as the scope fence, which agrees with ① item 2.
- Check-runs on this head at 04:40:11Z: 49 listed. One completed failure, the superseded first `Check Changeset` job (122011379357); its re-run is success. Success since the prior record's reading: every Lint lane (`Lint · CI, release & engine gates` carries the teardown-shape self-test, lint.yml:3931), `Type Check · source gates` (carries `check:generated --reconcile-only`, lint.yml:5293, so the generated export.mdx is CI-fresh on this head), Build Docs, Plan Test Core shards, `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Check Documentation Links` and `Dogfood Regression Gate`. Still in progress: Build Core, Build UI Deps, Test Core shards 1 to 8, `Type Check · consumer gates` (`check:doc-formula-expressions`, lint.yml:6472), `Type Check · debt ledger` and `Type Check · workspace` (`check:docs-transcript-drift`, lint.yml:5780). Not all green yet; the landing waits on the in-progress lanes, not on this record.
